title: Astor vs. Origin: which AI financial advisor fits you?
summary: Origin is an all-in-one money app with an AI Advisor. Astor is a personal investing agent that watches what you own. Here’s how to choose.
body_markdown:
## What’s the difference between Astor and Origin?


Origin is built to be the one place you manage money. You connect your bank, card, loan and investment accounts through Plaid, MX or Finicity, and Origin gives you a budget, a spending view, your net worth and a forecasting tool for big decisions like buying a home or retiring earlier. It also offers its own products, including automated investing, themed stock bundles, a cash account and a basic will, and you can invite a partner at no extra cost.


Origin’s AI Advisor sits on top of that data. You can ask it questions in plain English, model “what if” scenarios and get personalized guidance. It also works proactively, running what Origin calls expert-built checks across spending, savings, investments, retirement, credit, protection, housing, education and estate planning. The results show up as a Financial Health Score and a prioritized list of Actions, each with the reasoning behind it. If you want a person, Origin also sells financial planning sessions with its own planners as a premium service.


Astor goes narrower and deeper. It’s a[personal investing agent](https://www.astor.app/blog/what-is-a-personal-investing-agent) that connects to your brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts, learns what you own, and watches the market for what matters to your portfolio. When something crosses a line you care about, it texts you what happened, why it matters to you and what you could do. You can text it back in[iMessage](https://www.astor.app/blog/talk-to-astor-in-imessage) , check[At a glance](https://www.astor.app/blog/at-a-glance) for two lines on what moved your money today, or set[scheduled alerts](https://www.astor.app/blog/scheduled-alerts) for things like a check-in after a company you own reports earnings.


Put simply, Origin looks across your whole financial picture, and Astor looks closely at what you own.
